First, we note that 

$$
F(t)=\int {F}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t=\int ⟨{csc}^{2}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\text{d}t.
$$

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨{csc}^{2}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\text{d}t & =⟨\int {csc}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t,\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cot}⁡t+{c}_{1},\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cot}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩+⟨{c}_{1},\,{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cot}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩+C,\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $C$ is an arbitrary (vector) constant of integration.
